newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Hills gets buy rating.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Hills gets buy rating.

text.p: Diversified manufacturer Hills Industries Ltd was being recommended as a buy, reflecting a sound financial position and a potential for further trading improvement, Morgan Stockbroking Ltd said.

"Recommendation is a buy. The company has performed relatively well in difficult conditions and should benefit from a pick-up in Australian housing activity," Morgan analyst Greg Cathro said in an investment report.
Hills was becoming an increasingly diversified manufacturing company, complementing its historic housing-related products with expansion into communications technology-related areas, Cathro said.
Hills was forecasting further improvements in the current year ended June 30, 1997, Cathro said.

The consumer products division had lifted profitability but it was unlikely that strong growth would occur until well into 1997 when new products were introduced and a recovery in Australian housing may be underway, he said.
Economic improvement should also assist the industrial products and electronics divisions.
Cathro said Hills had been criticised for being involved in too many businesses and that some were too small.
"However, the recent sale of the Telefix division indicates that the company is rationalising to concentrate on those areas with most potential," Cathro said.

He said diversification of operations proved beneficial in 1995/96 as gains by the electronics division more than offset a static result from industrial products and a downturn in the consumer products division.
A forecast price-earnings ratio for Hills of 13.6 compared well with other housing related stocks such as Boral Ltd , with a price earnings of 22.2, and Email Ltd (19.2), he said.
"The company has a sound financial position and is on the lookout for acquisitions which reinforce its diversification, particularly into overseas markets," Cathro said.
Hills shares were unchanged at A$1.70 in opening trade on Tuesday.
